script: When Klay Thompson signed a two-year deal with the Heat, the immediate connection fans made was Ray Allen 2.0. To be fair, there are similarities here. Both players are three-point shooting legends who come from a championship pedigree on the back end of their career to play a limited but important bench role to help space the floor and make big clutch shots when the time is right. As far as the numbers go, Allen was 37 and 38 during his time with Miami. The last two years of his 18-year career, and despite that, he still managed to play 79 and 73 games in each of the seasons and then put up a solid 10 points per game on roughly 40% three-point shooting. Klay Thompson is currently 36, so about a year younger, and just came off of a 12 point-per-game season in Dallas, playing 69 games on 38% three-point shooting. Klay himself says he's motivated to have a redemption season, so it's possible he can make a big splash with the Yiannis and Bans, who's getting most of the opposing defense's attention, but he is most likely going to come off the bench as a veteran guy behind Tim Hardaway Jr. and Andrew Wiggins.
